task.description:
REWORK ITERATION 2 on the ISS-0911 design. CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's fresh re-check (handoffs/WF03-ISS0911-20260930/step-02b-code-design-validator-recheck1.json's result.summary/issues -- read in full) found rework 1's merged effect genuinely closes the original two-effect race, but its lookupWroteDefinitionId guard is a PERSISTENT, non-expiring token (only ever overwritten, never cleared/consumed) -- so a definitionId value the effect wrote once can be wrongly mistaken for a fresh self-write arbitrarily later if an unrelated EXTERNAL definitionId change happens to revisit that same value (e.g. found('Alice') writes ref=aliceId -> dialog closes -> external change to bobId updates correctly (ref untouched, still aliceId) -> a LATER external change back to aliceId wrongly matches the stale ref, so the guard skips updating and startDefinitionVersion/startDefinitionId stay stuck at Bob's stale data). Also: the design never specifies resetting the guard on dialog open/close, letting it leak across dialog sessions.

Fix required: make lookupWroteDefinitionId a ONE-SHOT/EXPIRING guard -- either (a) consume and clear it the FIRST time step 3 checks it (so it can only ever suppress exactly one re-trigger, the one it itself caused, never a later coincidental id match), or (b) replace the bare id-equality check with a generation/render-token comparison (a monotonically incrementing counter bumped every time the effect's found-branch runs, compared against a captured value, never matched by an unrelated later event). State explicitly which you chose and why the other was rejected. Also specify that the guard/token is reset whenever the dialog closes and re-opens, so no state survives across dialog sessions. Update lib/letflow/design/iss0911-start-instance-dialog-exact-lookup.md.

This is rework iteration 2 of 3. If this fails a third time for a RELATED root cause (guard/token design), the next dispatch must change approach entirely (e.g. abandon the ref-guard pattern altogether in favor of routing the lookup-driven id through the SAME state-setting path as the external-definitionId path, so there is structurally only one writer and no guard is needed at all) rather than patching the guard shape again.
acceptance_criteria: the fix calls definitionsApi.getActive(name) (or an equivalent exact-match backend lookup) keyed on the dialog's own typed value, not the page-level filtered list
a race-guard against out-of-order async responses (rapid typing) is explicitly designed, not left implicit
the version field's loading/not-found/found states are all specified

a single write path for startDefinitionVersion/startDefinitionId is designed, with no possibility of the new effect's own setSearchParams call re-triggering a second, independent effect that transiently desyncs the two values

NEW (this rework): the guard/token distinguishing a self-caused definitionId change from an external one is one-shot/expiring (or generation-token based), cannot be revived by an unrelated later event reaching the same id value, and is reset on dialog open/close

result.summary: Rewrote lib/letflow/design/iss0911-start-instance-dialog-exact-lookup.md's §5.2 to make lookupWroteDefinitionId a one-shot/expiring guard (option (a)): step 3 now reads-then-immediately-clears the ref every time it runs, unconditionally, so a value it ever held can match on at most one subsequent effect run -- it can never be revived by an unrelated later definitionId change coincidentally reaching the same id value (the exact bug step-02b-code-design-validator-recheck1.json found). Option (b) (generation/render-token counter) was explicitly considered and rejected in a new top-of-doc 'Rework 2' section: the merged effect's dependency array ([definitionId, activeDefinitionByName?.id, activeDefinitionByName?.version, versionLookupState]) only ever allows exactly one effect run to observe a self-written definitionId before activeDefinitionByName resolves for it (making the guard moot) or versionLookupState routes the next run to steps 1/2 instead of step 3 -- so a one-shot consumed-on-first-check guard is sufficient and simpler than a counter. Also specified: openStartDialog and closeStartDialog (InstanceBoardPage.tsx lines 223-238) both now clear lookupWroteDefinitionId.current on open/close as defense-in-depth (not load-bearing given the one-shot consumption, but keeps 'no guard state outlives its dialog session' true by construction too). Added a second invariant-check paragraph to §5.2 and a new AC-map row. No implementation code added -- guard logic specified in prose plus the existing ref's type signature only.
result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR for a fresh full pass
